title_en: Supreme People's Court Releases Six Typical Cases of Infringement of Intellectual Property Rights and Manufacturing and Selling Counterfeit and Shoddy Goods
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Published Six Typical Cases of Intellectual Property Infringement and Manufacturing and Selling Counterfeit and Substandard Goods

To support the national special campaign against intellectual property infringement and the manufacturing and selling of counterfeit and substandard goods, to deter lawbreakers, effectively protect intellectual property, and maintain the order of the socialist market economy, the Supreme People's Court published six typical cases of intellectual property infringement and manufacturing and selling counterfeit and substandard goods:

1. Defendants Huang Conglin, Ding Ping, Zhang Zhimin, and twelve others, and Defendant Unit Shenzhen Dingsheng International Freight Forwarding Co., Ltd. — Case of Selling Counterfeit and Substandard Products

The Intermediate People's Court of Dongguan City, Guangdong Province, found through trial: From April 2005, defendants Huang Conglin and Ding Ping successively rented warehouses in Humen Town and Chang'an Town of Dongguan City, and Pinghu Town of Shenzhen City, and successively employed defendants Luo Xiang, Che Shuxian, Chen Zhongwu, Su Jianglong, Chen Bingzhu, Chen Zhangming, Che Haoxian, and others to provide storage, transit, contact for booking space, and customs declaration services for others exporting counterfeit cigarettes. Defendants Zhang Zhimin, Wu Guowu, and Tang Yi (separately prosecuted) negotiated the fees for exporting counterfeit cigarettes with Huang Conglin and Ding Ping, then, entrusted by the cargo owners, arranged for the transportation of counterfeit cigarettes from Yunxiao County, Zhangpu County, and other places in Fujian Province to the aforesaid warehouses, and provided bank accounts to transfer payments from the cargo owners to Huang Conglin. Ding Ping was responsible for instructing Che Shuxian and others to unload counterfeit cigarettes into warehouses or load them into containers, and entrusted defendants Fang Weiqun and Lu Duzheng to handle customs declaration procedures in the name of exporting ordinary goods, shipping the counterfeit cigarettes by sea to the United Kingdom, Germany, Egypt, the United Arab Emirates, and other countries and regions for sale. Defendant Wu Shengcai was employed to engage in the transit management of counterfeit cigarettes at a warehouse in the Maxiang Industrial Park, Huaide Tianxin Village, Humen Town. According to statistics, from December 2005 to June 2008, Huang Conglin and Ding Ping participated in the transit of counterfeit and substandard cigarettes valued at RMB 153,618,786; Luo Xiang, Chen Zhongwu, Che Shuxian, and Su Jianglong handled involved amounts of RMB 149,169,286; Chen Bingzhu, Chen Zhangming, and Che Haoxian handled involved amounts of RMB 119,160,160, RMB 87,808,660, and RMB 7,697,160 respectively; Zhang Zhimin handled an involved amount of RMB 30,335,726; Wu Shengcai handled an involved amount of RMB 686,126; Wu Guowu handled an involved amount of RMB 577,500; Lu Duzheng handled an involved amount of RMB 49,798,500; Fang Weiqun handled an involved amount of RMB 22,206,250; defendant Peng Hongyan, as the legal representative of Dingsheng Company, after the end of April 2008, knowing that the goods Ding Ping entrusted for booking space were counterfeit cigarettes, still continued to accept such entrustment to help book space, handling an involved amount of RMB 17,258,000. The counterfeit cigarettes involved included counterfeit foreign brand cigarettes such as BENSON & HEDGES, MARLBORO, SUPERKINGS, DAVIDOFF, BRINGI, MONTANA, ARDATH, CAMEL, DUNHILL, 555, PALL MALL, FREE, BRISTOL, MORELLO, LUFFMAN, LAMBERT & BUTLER, and counterfeit domestic brand cigarettes such as FURONGWANG, BAISHA, and ZHONGHUA.

The Intermediate People's Court of Dongguan City determined that all defendants in this case constituted the crime of selling counterfeit and substandard products, with Huang Conglin and Ding Ping being principals, and Huang Conglin and Luo Xiang having meritorious performance. Based on the criminal circumstances of each defendant, the court sentenced defendant Huang Conglin to fifteen years' imprisonment and a fine of RMB 5,000,000; sentenced defendant Ding Ping to fifteen years' imprisonment and a fine of RMB 2,000,000; sentenced defendant Zhang Zhimin to thirteen years' imprisonment and a fine of RMB 1,000,000; and sentenced the remaining defendants to imprisonment ranging from nine years to one year and six months, and fines ranging from RMB 700,000 to RMB 20,000. After the judgment was pronounced, nine defendants including Huang Conglin appealed. The High People's Court of Guangdong Province, after trial, rejected the appeal and affirmed the original judgment.

2. Defendants Zheng Chenglai and Cui Chengquan — Case of Selling Goods Bearing Counterfeit Registered Trademarks

The Intermediate People's Court of Qingdao City, Shandong Province, found through trial: In July 2007, defendant Zheng Chenglai (South Korean nationality) entrusted defendant Cui Chengquan, who was engaged in transportation intermediary services, to transport 90,000 tablets of counterfeit "Viagra" (bearing the registered trademark of Pfizer Inc., USA) and counterfeit "Cialis" (bearing the registered trademark of Eli Lilly and Company, USA) to South Korea for sale. Cui Chengquan, knowing that the goods sold by Zheng Chenglai were goods bearing counterfeit registered trademarks, still assisted in transportation and entrusted the drugs to a logistics company in the name of the cargo owner to clear customs under the name of women's knitted underwear. On July 13, 2007, the above goods were seized by Qingdao Dagang Customs of the People's Republic of China during customs clearance due to suspected false declaration of product names. Upon appraisal, the price per tablet of "Viagra" and "Cialis" was RMB 107 and RMB 123.75 respectively.

The Intermediate People's Court of Qingdao City determined that defendants Zheng Chenglai and Cui Chengquan both constituted the crime of selling goods bearing counterfeit registered trademarks. Zheng Chenglai was the principal, but considering the attempted crime and that during the trial, he voluntarily paid the fine through relatives and had a good attitude of admitting guilt, he was given a mitigated punishment: sentenced to two years' imprisonment and a fine of RMB 500,000, and to be deported. Defendant Cui Chengquan was an accessory, and the crime was attempted, so he was given a mitigated punishment: sentenced to one year and eight months' imprisonment and a fine of RMB 200,000 for the crime of selling goods bearing counterfeit registered trademarks. After the judgment was pronounced, none of the defendants appealed, and the judgment became legally effective.

3. Defendant Yang Changjun — Case of Selling Goods Bearing Counterfeit Registered Trademarks

The People's Court of Chaoyang District, Beijing, found through trial: Starting in May 2007, defendant Yang Changjun stored men's and women's bags bearing the registered trademarks of LOUIS VUITTON, GUCCI, and CHANEL in a warehouse on the third underground floor of Xiushui Market, Chaoyang District, Beijing, for sale and profit. On August 9, 2009, public security officers seized from this warehouse 8,425 men's and women's bags bearing the registered trademarks of LOUIS VUITTON, GUCCI, and CHANEL, with a total value of RMB 766,990.

The People's Court of Chaoyang District determined that defendant Yang Changjun constituted the crime of selling goods bearing counterfeit registered trademarks. Considering the attempted crime and his admission of guilt and repentance after the incident, he was given a lighter punishment: sentenced to three years and six months' imprisonment and a fine of RMB 10,000; the 8,425 bags bearing counterfeit registered trademarks were ordered to be confiscated. After the judgment was pronounced, Yang Changjun appealed. The Second Intermediate People's Court of Beijing, after trial, rejected Yang Changjun's appeal and affirmed the original judgment.

4. Defendant Jin Fusong — Case of Counterfeiting Registered Trademarks

The People's Court of Jin'an District, Fuzhou City, found through trial: Starting from August 6, 2008, defendant Jin Fusong, in collusion with Lin Zhixiang (at large), without authorization from the owners of the registered trademarks, produced and sold toner bearing nine registered trademarks including Canon, Toshiba, Minolta, Kyocera, Xerox, Ricoh, Sharp, Panasonic, and Aurora for profit. By the time the case was discovered on March 4, 2009, the amount of various types of counterfeit toner sold was RMB 183,566, and there were 1,771 pieces of counterfeit toner not yet sold. Among these, 1,769 pieces had a total value of RMB 112,611 based on the marked price or the actual average sales price of the infringing products that had been ascertained.

The People's Court of Jin'an District found defendant Jin Fusong guilty of the crime of counterfeiting registered trademarks and sentenced him to four years' imprisonment and a fine of RMB 150,000. After the judgment was pronounced, Jin Fusong appealed. The Intermediate People's Court of Fuzhou City, after trial, rejected Jin Fusong's appeal and affirmed the original judgment.

5. Defendant Hori Shigeru — Case of Infringement of Trade Secrets

The Intermediate People's Court of Chengdu City, Sichuan Province, found through trial: In October 1994, Japan Mikuni Corporation and Sichuan Xiguang Industry (Group) Company jointly invested to establish the Sino-foreign joint venture Chengdu Mikuni Company to produce and sell carburetors and related products for engines. The secondary air valve was the main product of Chengdu Mikuni Company. From May 21, 1999, to September 1, 2004, defendants Hori Shigeru (Japanese nationality), Zhou Yong, Liu Fagang, and Shen Qian held positions at Chengdu Mikuni Company as general manager, section chief of the development division of the technology department, section chief of manufacturing technology of the production department, and Japanese translator and related work for Hori Shigeru, respectively. During his tenure as general manager, Hori Shigeru directly kept the relevant drawings that Chengdu Mikuni Company claimed constituted trade secrets. Zhou Yong and Liu Fagang, during their tenure, had access to drawings of the secondary air valve of Chengdu Mikuni Company. In September 2004, Hori Shigeru was recalled to Japan by Japan Mikuni Corporation. Before returning to Japan, Hori Shigeru discussed with defendant Lei Jianping the separate establishment of Jiangmen Kemei Electromechanical Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Kemei Company), deciding that Lei Jianping would contribute the capital and act as the actual controller and be responsible for product sales. Hori Shigeru recommended to Lei Jianping that Chengdu Mikuni Company employees Zhou Yong, Liu Fagang, and Shen Qian work at Kemei Company. From September to December 2004, Shen Qian, Zhou Yong, and Liu Fagang successively resigned from Chengdu Mikuni Company and participated in the preparation of Kemei Company. After Kemei Company was registered and established, they assumed positions there. In May 2005, Kemei Company began producing and selling secondary air valves. During this period, Hori Shigeru, through Shen Qian, requested Liu Fagang, who had not yet resigned, to secretly photograph the secondary air valve equipment of Chengdu Mikuni Company and send the photos to Hori Shigeru via email. Zhou Yong asked Zhao Zehui, a technician at Chengdu Mikuni Company, to mail relevant parts of the secondary air valve to Kemei Company. Hori Shigeru copied the technical drawings of the secondary air valve that he had obtained during his tenure at Chengdu Mikuni Company to Zhou Yong. Based on the above materials, Zhou Yong drew the secondary air valve drawings at Kemei Company. Kemei Company manufactured and sold 841,084 units of secondary air valve Model AV01 based on these drawings.

The Intermediate People's Court of Chengdu City determined that defendants Hori Shigeru, Lei Jianping, Zhou Yong, Liu Fagang, and Shen Qian violated the confidentiality requirements of Chengdu Mikuni Company by stealing, disclosing, and using the trade secrets they had acquired, causing significant losses of RMB 2,355,035.2 to Chengdu Mikuni Company. Their actions constituted the crime of infringement of trade secrets. The court sentenced Hori Shigeru to two years and five months' imprisonment and a fine of RMB 500,000; sentenced Lei Jianping, Zhou Yong, and Liu Fagang to two years' imprisonment with three years' probation and a fine of RMB 400,000; and sentenced Shen Qian to one year's imprisonment with two years' probation and a fine of RMB 100,000. After the judgment was pronounced, Hori Shigeru and others appealed. The High People's Court of Sichuan Province, after trial, rejected the appeals of all appellants and affirmed the original judgment.

6. Wang Jiahao — Case of Copyright Infringement

The People's Court of Changshu City, Jiangsu Province, found through trial: Starting in March 2008, defendant Wang Jiahao, without approval, established the "7t7t Music" website (http://www.7t7t.com) on the internet to provide music listening services. This included 677 songs owned by members of the International Federation of the Phonographic Industry, including Universal Music Ltd., SONY MUSIC ENTERTAINMENT (HONG KONG) LIMITED, SONY MUSIC ENTERTAINMENT (TAIWAN) LTD., and Warner Music International Inc. Wang Jiahao had no legal rights to the songs provided for online listening. From March 2009 to June 2009, Wang Jiahao embedded advertisements on the website and obtained advertising revenue of RMB 12,837.05.

The People's Court of Changshu City determined that defendant Wang Jiahao, for the purpose of profit, without permission from the copyright owners, uploaded musical works copyrighted by others to the internet to provide listening services to internet users. The circumstances were serious, and his actions constituted the crime of copyright infringement. Considering that Wang Jiahao had voluntarily surrendered and showed repentance, he could be given a lighter punishment according to law, and since a suspended sentence would not cause further harm to society, the court sentenced Wang Jiahao to six months' imprisonment, suspended for one year, and a fine of RMB 15,000; criminal proceeds were ordered to be recovered. After the judgment was pronounced, the defendant Wang Jiahao did not appeal, and the procuratorial authority did not lodge a protest. The judgment has become legally effective.
